chats.answer:
For a 60,000W (60kW) solar generator, you're looking at a much larger system than a typical portable solar power station.

The best choice depends on whether you mean:

60,000W (60kW) output: Enough power for a large home, multiple buildings, or substantial equipment.

60,000Wh (60kWh) battery capacity: Enough stored energy to supply 2,500W continuously for approximately 24 hours, before conversion losses.

These are very different specifications. Most portable solar generators provide around 2,000–7,200W of continuous output, while larger expandable systems can reach much higher capacities.

chats.answer:
For a 60,000W (60kW) solar generator, you're looking at a much larger system than a typical portable power station. At this power level, the best options are usually modular home battery systems or commercial solar-plus-storage systems.

One important distinction:

60,000W (60kW) = power output, or how much equipment you can run simultaneously.

60,000Wh (60kWh) = battery capacity, or how much energy you can store.

A 60kWh battery could theoretically power a 3,000W load for 20 hours, before efficiency losses.
